_why_two_claims: AGREEMENT asks whether the engines compute the same thing; RECOVERY asks whether they compute the right thing. Neither implies the other.

truth.source: the fixture's data-generating process: Laplace changes, symmetric about +3

agreement.claim: both engines report the same pseudo-median, exact interval, V statistic and exact p-value
agreement._note: Observed spread on the committed fixture: 0 at ten significant digits on every key. harness/comparisons_examples.test.py checks that the null distribution Python builds totals 2^45 and reproduces scipy's exact p-value, and that scipy's own statistic (min(W+, W-) = 228) is not R's V.

recovery.claim: the pseudo-median change is close to the centre the fixture was built with

calibration.limits: Measured by harness/comparisons_examples.test.py over seeds 0 to 99 of this generator. Laplace changes have heavy tails, which is why the spread is wide for 45 pairs.

r: wilcox.test(d$after, d$before, paired = TRUE, exact = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE
